titulo: Module 06 — Quiz: the agentic loop, hooks, and handoff

questoes.pergunta: Which field of the Messages API response should decide whether the agentic loop continues or ends?
opcoes: The last `text` block in `content`, looking for signals such as "done"
The `stop_reason`
The number of blocks in `content`
`usage.output_tokens` compared with `max_tokens`
questoes.explicacao: `stop_reason` is the API contract: `tool_use` → execute and continue; `end_turn` → finished. Text is ambiguous and is not a stop signal.
feedbacks: Classic anti-pattern #1: deciding when to stop by reading natural language. The model can write "all set" and still request a tool in the same turn.
Correct. `stop_reason` is the structured signal that drives the loop.
Counting blocks tells you nothing: a final response can have a single block, and one with tools can have several.
Comparing tokens would only help detect truncation, and `stop_reason: max_tokens` already exists for that.

questoes.pergunta: The response came back with `stop_reason: "max_tokens"`. What does this indicate?
opcoes: The model finished normally and used exactly its budget
The context window filled up
The response was cut off at the output ceiling and is incomplete
A server-side tool hit its iteration cap
questoes.explicacao: `max_tokens` = it was cut off at the OUTPUT limit, mid-response. Continue the generation or raise the ceiling; never treat it as complete.
feedbacks: Finishing normally is `end_turn`. `max_tokens` means truncation, not completion.
A full window before reaching the output ceiling is `model_context_window_exceeded`, a different value.
Correct. The output is truncated (cut-off JSON, a half-finished sentence).
That's `pause_turn`, tied to server-side tool loops.

questoes.pergunta: Your agent uses the server-side web search tool, and the response arrives with `stop_reason: "pause_turn"`. What should you do?
opcoes: Resend the conversation, appending the response as an assistant turn, so the model can continue
Treat it as an error and abort the task
Build a `tool_result` for the web search and send it back
Stop and show the partial text as the final answer
questoes.explicacao: `pause_turn` = the server-side loop hit its iteration cap. Resend so the model picks up where it left off.
feedbacks: Correct. Just resend with the response appended; the model continues the work.
It's not an error: it's a pause anticipated by the protocol.
Server-side tools are executed by Anthropic; you don't build a `tool_result` for them.
The task isn't finished. Showing the partial text as final delivers incomplete work.

questoes.pergunta: Why can code that only checks for `HTTP 200` treat a safety refusal as an "empty success"?
opcoes: Because refusals come with HTTP 400 and the code doesn't handle 400
Because the refusal only appears in the response header
Because the refusal comes as a special `tool_use` block
Because the refusal arrives with HTTP 200 and `stop_reason: "refusal"`
questoes.explicacao: A refusal is a valid API response (HTTP 200). Only by looking at `stop_reason` can you distinguish it from a normal response.
feedbacks: A refusal isn't an HTTP error; if it were a 400, code that checks for 200 wouldn't even treat it as a success.
The refusal is signaled in the body, via `stop_reason`, not via a header.
There's no refusal `tool_use`; the signal is `stop_reason: refusal`.
Correct. That's why you check `stop_reason` before reading `content`.

questoes.pergunta: A response's `content` has a `text` block ("I'll look up your order.") and a `tool_use` block. What should the loop do?
opcoes: Show the text to the user and stop, since there's already a text response
Execute the tool, return the `tool_result`, and continue the loop
Discard the text and resend, asking only for the `tool_use`
Ask the model to choose between responding and calling the tool
questoes.explicacao: Mixed text and `tool_use` are normal. The `stop_reason` will be `tool_use`: execute and continue. Having text doesn't mean it's finished.
feedbacks: Classic mistake: having text isn't a signal of completion. The requested tool would never be executed.
Correct. The text is narration; the `tool_use` is the requested action.
Mixed content is valid, and the text should remain in the history.
The model has already decided: it called the tool. There's no choice to redo.

questoes.pergunta: The model requested three tools in the same response. How should the results come back?
opcoes: Three `user` messages, one per result, in order of execution
Only the first tool's result; the model will ask for the others later
A single `user` message with three `tool_result` blocks, each with the exact `tool_use_id`
A single `tool_result` concatenating the three outputs
questoes.explicacao: Parallel tool use: all `tool_result` blocks go in a single `user` message, each matched by the request's `tool_use_id`.
feedbacks: Spreading results across several `user` messages breaks the protocol.
Every `tool_use` needs a response; a missing result causes an error.
Correct. One result per request, exact ids, one message.
Concatenating loses the link between each request and its result.

questoes.pergunta: A tool timed out. What is the right way to inform the model?
opcoes: Return a `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and a message explaining the failure
Omit that tool's `tool_result` so as not to confuse the model
Return a `tool_result` with empty content, as if there were no data
Throw an exception and restart the conversation from scratch
questoes.explicacao: The failure also gets a result, with `is_error: true`, so the model can reason about recovery (retry, another tool, escalate).
feedbacks: Correct. An explicit error lets the model decide how to recover.
Omitting the result breaks the protocol and hides the problem.
Empty as success is silent suppression: the model concludes "there's no data" when the lookup never even ran.
Aborting everything over one failure wastes the work already done; the model can recover.

questoes.pergunta: A team configured the loop to stop after exactly 5 iterations on every task. What is the problem?
opcoes: None, as long as the number is chosen based on the historical average
The problem is only cost: 5 iterations are too expensive
Iteration limits are forbidden in any form
A fixed limit as the primary criterion cuts off long tasks and doesn't reflect the real end; it should only be a backstop
questoes.explicacao: An arbitrary limit as the primary stopping mechanism is an anti-pattern. A high cap as a backstop (with an alert) is acceptable; the normal end is `end_turn`.
feedbacks: The average doesn't solve it: tasks above it would be cut off midway.
The problem isn't cost, it's correctness: the stopping criterion is arbitrary.
An overstatement: as a safety net against infinite loops, a cap is correct.
Correct. As a backstop, yes; as a stopping criterion, no.

questoes.pergunta: What is the essential difference between a task budget and `max_tokens`?
opcoes: Task budget applies per response; `max_tokens` applies to the entire task
Task budget is visible to the model, which organizes itself to fit; `max_tokens` is invisible and cuts off midway
The two are equivalent; only the name changes
`max_tokens` limits the input; task budget limits the output
questoes.explicacao: Task budget [volatile, beta] is a task-level budget that the model sees and respects by planning. `max_tokens` is a per-response output ceiling that the model doesn't see.
feedbacks: Reversed: `max_tokens` is per response; the budget is for the task.
Correct. Visible (it organizes) vs. invisible (it cuts off).
They're not equivalent: the behavior when the limit is reached is the opposite.
`max_tokens` is an output ceiling, not an input ceiling.

questoes.pergunta: A team needs an agent with 4 internal tools, no file access, no subagents, and no resumable sessions. What is the most appropriate way to build it?
opcoes: Claude Agent SDK, since it's the most complete
Managed Agents, to avoid writing code
A manual loop on the Messages API, or the SDK's Tool Runner
An orchestrator with one subagent per tool
questoes.explicacao: Choose the simplest approach that meets the need. Without hooks, subagents, sessions, or file tools, a manual loop/Tool Runner is enough.
feedbacks: The Agent SDK brings Claude Code's entire harness; here that's unnecessary complexity.
Managed Agents are for when you don't want to operate the execution/sandbox; the question doesn't call for that.
Correct. The simplest one that solves the problem.
One subagent per tool is unnecessary decomposition for 4 tools.

questoes.pergunta: A rule says refunds may only be processed after identity has been verified. How do you guarantee it?
opcoes: Programmatic enforcement, such as a `PreToolUse` hook or a prerequisite inside the refund tool
Repeat the rule in capital letters in the system prompt and in the user message
Add three few-shot examples of verification before the refund
A second model that reviews the conversation before each refund
questoes.explicacao: A rule with financial consequences requires a deterministic guarantee: code (hook/prerequisite). Prompts, few-shot, and an LLM reviewer are probabilistic.
feedbacks: Correct. Deterministic: without verification, the tool doesn't run.
Emphasis in the prompt lowers the failure rate, but doesn't bring it to zero.
Few-shot improves the average; it's not a guarantee.
Another LLM is still probabilistic and adds cost and latency.

questoes.pergunta: In a `command`-type `PreToolUse` hook, the script ends with exit code 2. What happens?
opcoes: The tool runs normally and the error is only logged
The entire session is terminated
The hook is ignored and the next hook decides
The tool is blocked and stderr goes back to Claude as the reason
questoes.explicacao: Exit 0 passes; exit 2 blocks and sends stderr back to Claude, which reads the reason and adjusts. Other codes are a non-blocking error.
feedbacks: That's the behavior of other exit codes (non-blocking error), not of 2.
What's blocked is the action, not the session; Claude keeps working.
Exit 2 has its own meaning: block.
Correct. Blocking with feedback to the model.

questoes.pergunta: You want a CRM tool's result to reach the model with the card number masked. Which hook event should you use?
opcoes: `PreToolUse`
`PostToolUse`
`UserPromptSubmit`
`Stop`
questoes.explicacao: `PostToolUse` runs after the tool and is the place to normalize, clean up, and annotate the result (e.g., mask PII).
feedbacks: `PreToolUse` acts before execution; the result doesn't exist yet.
Correct. Post-execution, handling what the model will see.
`UserPromptSubmit` handles the user's prompt, not tool output.
`Stop` fires when the agent is about to end its turn.

questoes.pergunta: A hook needs to apply to every developer in the repository. Where should you configure it?
opcoes: Each developer's `~/.claude/settings.json`
`.claude/settings.local.json`
The project's `.claude/settings.json`, versioned in git
In CLAUDE.md, as an instruction
questoes.explicacao: Project settings (`.claude/settings.json`) are shared via git. `settings.local.json` is personal and gitignored; `~/.claude` belongs to the user.
feedbacks: It would require each person to configure it manually; nothing guarantees everyone will.
The `.local` file is personal and stays out of git.
Correct. Project = shared with the team.
CLAUDE.md is an instruction (probabilistic); it doesn't run hooks.

questoes.pergunta: Which items should be included in a support agent's handoff to a human representative? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: The complete, unedited transcript, so nothing is lost
The actions the agent has already taken and the reason for the escalation
The model's self-reported confidence level in its own analysis
The customer's identity (and whether it has been verified), the problem, and the recommended action
The customer's sentiment score as the main justification
questoes.explicacao: Handoff = a structured summary: customer/verification, problem, request, root cause, actions taken, why it was escalated, recommended action, amount.
feedbacks: A raw transcript forces the human to reread everything; the goal is to highlight what matters.
Correct. It keeps the human from repeating what has already been done.
Self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated; it's not a basis for decisions.
Correct. Identity, problem, and recommendation are the core of the handoff.
Sentiment is neither an escalation criterion nor central information about the case.
